text:
anya: quick heads-up — I ran a 4h shadowprof across a subset of H100 pods to compare the Triton vs CUTLASS routing when KV hits are low (hit < 30%).
chris: nice. what's the sampling rate and what traffic?
anya: 10% shadow routing, production traffic for the small-chat service, seqlen mix skewed to 8/16 (~72%) and a smaller tail at 64.
sana: did you keep batching config identical? that can hide differences.
anya: yep same batching windows and max_batch, only router was allowed to prefer different kernels. logs attached below (snips).
perf-bot: run summary: requests=120k, shadow_rate=0.10, duration=4h, pkgs:H100-a
chris: top-level observations?
anya: CUTLASS path wins median by ~6ms for seqlen<=16 when kv_hit_rate>0.5, but under kv_hit_rate<0.3 CUTLASS p99 spikes badly (sometimes +120ms). Triton is more stable on tail when KV cold.
sana: interesting. could be that CUTLASS has more aggressive kernel fusion that assumes contiguous KV cache — cold KV forces async reads that blow up latency.
anya: exactly. sample trace:
```
[trace] req=0x7fa3 seqlen=8 kv_hit=false chosen=cutlass latency=234ms
[trace] kv_fetch wait=160ms io_wait=145ms kernel_exec=20ms
[trace] req=0x8bc seqlen=8 kv_hit=true chosen=cutlass latency=12ms
```
chris: that io_wait in cold case is the killer. Triton seems to fallback to an execution plan that tolerates kv fetchs better.
anya: i also captured router.telemetry with the new tags: router.choice, kv.estimated_hit, probe.delta_ms. heatmap shows CUTLASS chosen 63% overall but that drops to 28% when estimated_hit<0.4.
sana: does the router currently use hysteresis? we saw oscillation last quarter.
anya: there is a soft_preference + fallback_penalty_ms=10ms. i bumped fallback_penalty_ms to 25ms locally and oscillation reduced but p99 for some bursts increased — tradeoff.
chris: any insight from kernel-level metrics (smem / active warps)?
anya: yes: CUTLASS kernel shows ~30% more shared mem pressure at batch>32 with short seqlen and cold kv, which increases warp stalls. Triton uses smaller kernels w/ more sequential KV overlapping, so stalls are amortized.
sana: so for autotune we might need sequence-aware cost functions that include kv_hit_estimate and batch_smearing metric.
anya: proposal: add a probe stage that runs microbenchmarks per pool with a controlled KV miss rate to get per-kernel cost surfaces. config example i hacked:
```
router.autotune:
  probe_sample_rate: 0.02
  probe_modes:
    - name: kv_cold
      kv_miss_target: 0.4
      trials: 50
    - name: kv_warm
      kv_miss_target: 0.05
      trials: 50
  metrics: [latency_median, latency_p99, kernel_sm_stall, io_wait_ms]
```
perf-bot: note: probe_sample_rate 2% on heavy endpoints may impact SLOs — run off-peak or in canary.
chris: agree. we should run this in canary capacity not production. canary plan?
anya: canary suggestion — route 5% live traffic + 100% shadow for another variant. cfg snippet:
```
routing.canary:
  keep_live_fraction: 0.05
  shadow_fraction: 0.20
  duration: 6h
  metrics_to_report: [router.choice, latency_p50, latency_p99, kv_hit_estimate]
```
sana: also add a new telemetry label: kernel_EXEC_HINT={cutlass,triton} and kv_context={hot,warm,cold} so we can slice easily.
anya: added that to the probe PR. quick raw numbers from run: overall p50 cutlass=11ms triton=17ms; p99 cutlass=210ms triton=55ms on cold segments. warm segments both under 30ms.
chris: those numbers justify a fallback policy based on estimated_kv. we could add rule: prefer CUTLASS if est_kv>0.45 and seqlen<=16 and batch<=32. otherwise prefer TRITON.
sana: and make that a soft policy with fast rollback and telemetry alerts if p99 increases >40ms over baseline.
anya: implemented a canary config in the playground; i'll kick off a low-impact canary tonight 02:00 UTC. will post dashboard links when ready.
chris: thanks — can you also dump the probe raw CSV and a few perf counters? need to feed into Optimize for recommendation engine.
anya: will upload CSV to /shared/profiler/shadowprof/2109876543-anya.csv and ping here.
perf-bot: alert rule suggestion created: router.choice_p99_delta > 40ms -> paging oncall.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: 02:00 UTC, 5% live + 20% shadow, target pods: h100-a-pool.ETA: 6h.
sana: awesome. one more ask — include a small synthetic test that simulates kv_miss storms so we can reproduce locally.
anya: adding repro script to PR. short repro snippet:
```
# simulate kv miss flood
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do curl -sS -X POST $CANARY_ENDPOINT -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
```
chris: perfect. thanks anya. postmortem if we see a regression, but this looks like the right guardrails. :thumbsup:
anya: will follow up with dashboard and CSV. tagging @sana for visibility.
sana: thanks, will review probe metrics and roll the rule into Optimize if stable.
anya: closing for now — will report back after canary. :rocket:
